story: Unkulunkulu is regarded among the Zulu, Ndebele, and Swati people as an "old-old one," or ancestor figure. In family and tribal contexts, such ancestor figures (called Onkulunkulu in the plural) could be male or female, and were treated with great respect by their families. In a broader sense, Unkulunkulu also existed as a single, ancient figure, understood to be male, who was regarded as the ancestor of humanity, though this role received little attention. With the spread of Christianity among these people, Unkulunkulu came to be understood differently — no longer simply as an ancestor, but as a creator deity closely resembling the Christian God. In this newer form, Unkulunkulu originated from reeds. From these same reeds he then created humans and livestock. Everything else in creation he made afterward, without drawing on any original source material. After completing all of his creation, Unkulunkulu is said to have forgotten what he had made and abandoned his creations. No myths describe him beyond this point of creation.
blind: The ancestor figure is regarded among a group of related peoples as an "old-old one," or ancestor figure. In family and community contexts, such ancestor figures could be male or female, and were treated with great respect by their families. In a broader sense, the ancestor figure also existed as a single, ancient figure, understood to be male, who was regarded as the ancestor of humanity, though this role received little attention. With the spread of a foreign religion among these people, the ancestor figure came to be understood differently — no longer simply as an ancestor, but as a creator deity closely resembling the god of that foreign religion. In this newer form, the creator figure originated from reeds. From these same reeds he then created humans and a kind of livestock. Everything else in creation he made afterward, without drawing on any original source material. After completing all of his creation, the creator figure is said to have forgotten what he had made and abandoned his creations. No myths describe him beyond this point of creation.
title: Unkulunkulu
